result.note: Tested the Delhi High Court's trademark ruling against Google on keyword ads and its rejection of the intermediary defence. Skipped the appeal's page count and the corporate positioning.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, the Delhi High Court ruled on a trademark suit filed by bathroom fittings maker Hindware against Google. Consider the following statements about the ruling:
items: It found Google liable for trademark infringement through its AdWords keyword system.
It accepted Google's defence that it was only a passive intermediary in the ad auction.
It ordered Google to pay around INR 3 million in damages plus costs.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The second statement is wrong because the court rejected the passive-intermediary defence, holding that Google actively profits from the auction system. Hindware sued after rivals bought "Hindware" as a keyword so that their ads appeared when consumers searched for the brand. In July 2026, Google appealed the ruling.
questions.source: The court rejected Google’s passive-intermediary defence, finding that it actively profits from the auction system and cannot wash its hands of resulting infringement.
